title: Latency shape workbench: percentile comparison by model, route, and IO path
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an interactive workbench/dashboard that lets SREs and platform engineers compare latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) across model families and API routes while splitting by IO path (streaming vs non-streaming). The workbench should surface distribution shapes, tail behavior, sample traces, and a small set of lightweight derived metrics to aid root cause analysis without exploding metrics cardinality.
acceptance_criteria: A Grafana board (workbench) exists with selectors for model family, route, time window, and IO path (streaming|sync)
Percentile series for p50, p95, and p99 are plotted and can be overlaid for streaming vs sync
Each percentile panel includes a linkable trace sample (trace id) and a lightweight error histogram
Metrics pipeline emits io_mode label (streaming|sync) and a bounded request_shape tag; cardinality limits enforced via rollup
New trace hook injects route_id, model_id, io_mode, and kv_cache_hit into span metadata
Alerting examples documented: p95 > 350ms for 5m window (prod routes) and p99 > 1.5s for 1m window
Dashboard queries complete within SLAs (render time < 4s for 30m window) using pre-aggregations
updates: 2026-02-10: Ticket created during observability retro; scoped to avoid cardinality explosion by requiring bounded request_shape values
2026-02-18: Spike completed — evaluated two rollup strategies: pre-aggregation at ingestion vs Prometheus-style recording rules. Chose ingestion-side rollups for lower query latency.
2026-02-25: Tracing changes prototyped: added io_mode and route_id tags to top-level span. Early tests show minimal overhead (~0.8% CPU).
2026-03-02: UX mock uploaded to Confluence and reviewed by PM and Design. Feedback: emphasize time-overlaid comparison and make trace sample open in a side panel rather than a new tab.

2026-03-05: Engineering review - Diego to own metrics schema. Decided to cap model_family cardinality by using normalized families (e.g., 'llama-2-70b' -> 'llama-2-70b') and to bucket request_shape into 'short|medium|long'.
2026-03-09: PR opened to metrics pipeline (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6213) and tracing hook change (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1879).
2026-03-12: Integration tests for ingestion rollup merged to staging. Dashboard panels rendered from pre-aggregated indices with <2s query time in 30m window.
Next: complete alert tuning, add playbook entries, and schedule a canary with 2 production routes.
notes: Trade-off: ingestion-side rollups reduce query cost but increase storage of pre-aggregates; acceptable given SLO for dashboard latency.
We deliberately avoid labeling by exact model_version in dashboard selectors to prevent cardinality explosion; use model_family + pinned_version dropdown only for deep-dive flows.
Sampling policy: keep 1:1 tracing for production-critical routes; lower sampling (1:100) for bulk endpoints. Documented in runbook.
Potential follow-up: provide a small streaming-tail visual that animates token emission times for sampled streaming sessions. Blocked on frontend time-series renderer support.
review_feedback: PM Priya Patel: add an example of customer-facing regression scenario and how alerts tie to rollouts
Design Samir Gupta: prefer side-by-side percentile overlays with stacked area view for distribution
SRE Anna Müller: request to include kv_cache_hit rate as a correlated series to explain tail spikes
